ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a circle, points B and D are on the circumference, and segment BD is drawn as a straight line passing through the marked point E inside the circle; E is located at the center position of the circle. Reasoning: Because BD passes through center E and both endpoints are on the circumference, BD is the diameter of the circle. It is known that BD = 12 millimeters, and the radius equals half the diameter, so r = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 millimeters.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as showing E at the center of the circle, with B, E, and D collinear on segment BD. Since EB and ED go from the center to points on the circle, they are both radii and are equal. The text gives BD = 12, so EB + ED = 12. Let each radius be r; then r + r = 12, so 2r = 12 and r = 6 millimeters.
